newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu approves oil drilling on Golan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu approves oil drilling on Golan - paper.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu approved a request by a state-owned company to drill for oil on the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war, Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Friday.
Netanyahu spokesman Shai Bazak said he was checking the report.
Haaretz said the National Oil Company made the request.

It said, however, that actual drilling could be held up indefinitely, despite Netanyahu's approval in principle, by a recent decision to privatise the oil company. Legal reviews of the request have still to be completed, the daily said.
Nearly five years of sporadic peace talks between Israel and Syria have long stalled over the strategic heights.

Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal. Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May elections, was ready to make at least a partial withdrawal for full peace and normal ties with Syria.
Netanyahu rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace.
